deep.reconstruction:
This page is not by Riemann. It is the first page of a letter by H. A. Schwarz, dated Göttingen, 8 February 1876, to a 'Lieber College'. The addressee is most plausibly Hattendorff or Weber, who were preparing the minimal-surface material (Riemann's 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung') for Riemann's Werke (1876). The previous page in the bundle ends another letter signed by Schwarz. Schwarz returns a manuscript dealing with the 'ringförmige Minimalfläche' (doubly connected minimal surface) bounded by two plane polygons lying in parallel planes. He says its count of constants is inaccurate and gives the correct count.

Content in modern terms:

(1) Hypothesis that must be stated. The two given plane polygons must be convex and traversed once (turning number 1). The polygon angles are δ_μπ and δ'_νπ, with Σ(1-δ_μ) = 2 and Σ(1-δ'_ν) = 2 (next page). Under this hypothesis the following hold:
- The stereographic Gauss map η (Riemann's notation) takes the value η = 0 at every vertex of one polygon and η = ∞ at every vertex of the other.
- The Gauss map has no interior branch points. These are the singular tangent planes, 't = a' in the main treatise. The only singularities are the reversal points of the normal on the boundary ('t = b, b''). 
- The Gauss image covers the sphere exactly once.

My consistency check (not on the page): by Gauss–Bonnet on an annulus (χ = 0), ∫K dA + Σ(exterior angles) = 0. The exterior angles are π(1-δ) at each vertex, and the straight edges are geodesic. So ∫K dA = -π(2+2) = -4π, which is degree 1 of the Gauss map, i.e. a simple covering of the sphere. This agrees with Schwarz.

(2) Notation suggestion. The t-values at the vertices should be called c, c' as in the main treatise; Schwarz calls this a minor point.

(3) Constant count. The parameter surface T is the two-sheeted surface over the half-plane, with branch points (inserted: 'Doppel-') at t = +i and t = +i/k. This surface is conformally an annulus with modulus fixed by k. Its conformal self-maps (the 'reelle Transformation der Fläche T in sich') form only a one-parameter family; on the next page they are the translations v → v + const in v = ∫ dt/√((1+t²)(1+k²t²)), i.e. rotations of the annulus. Hence only one, not two, of the vertex parameters c_1…c_m, c'_1…c'_n can be normalized arbitrarily. Implied consequence (mine): the free conformal parameters are k plus (m+n-1) vertex positions.

The next page continues: d log η/dv is elliptic with periods 2K' and 4Ki, with residues δ_μ-1 and 1-δ'_ν. The additive constant must be fixed so that the integral over the core circle equals 2πi exactly. Requiring only a vanishing real part is insufficient.
errors: No mathematical error by the letter writer is visible on this page; the statements are consistent with Gauss–Bonnet and with the conformal automorphism group of an annulus being one-dimensional (rotations).
Attribution caution: the page is a letter by H. A. Schwarz (1876), written ten years after Riemann's death, criticising a manuscript by an editor; it should not be read as Riemann's own work.

results.what: Convex, once-traversed boundary polygons ensure the Gauss map of the minimal annulus is unbranched in the interior and covers the sphere exactly once (η=0 at all vertices of one polygon, ∞ at the other).
results.modern_name: Gauss map degree / total curvature -4π of a minimal annulus via Gauss–Bonnet; Weierstrass representation with polygonal boundary
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1867 posthumous), Schwarz, Weierstrass (Plateau problem for polygons, 1860s–1870s)

results.what: Correct count of constants: since the conformal self-maps of the doubly-connected parameter surface T form a 1-parameter family, only one vertex parameter may be normalized.
results.modern_name: Dimension of the moduli of an annulus / automorphism group of an annulus (rotations) in parameter counting for the Plateau problem
results.usually_credited_to: H. A. Schwarz (correction in this 1876 letter, reflected in the editorial notes of Riemann's Werke)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a letter by Schwarz from 1876 giving an editorial correction to the constant count in the posthumous treatment of Riemann's minimal annulus between two parallel polygons. It is mathematically routine for a specialist and is not Riemann's own work. It is of modest archival interest for the history of the edition of Riemann's Werke.

checkable.asserts: Gauss–Bonnet on the annulus: ∫K = -Σπ(1-δ) = -4π when Σ(1-δ_μ)=2 and Σ(1-δ'_ν)=2, i.e. the Gauss map has degree 1 (simple covering of the sphere).
For k=1/2, ∫_0^∞ dt/√((1+t²)(1+k²t²)) = K' = K(m=1-k²), so the real t-line maps to a segment of length 2K' in v (the rectangle width used on the next page); the difference should be ≈0.

checkable.sympy: Eq(sum([d-1 for d in [Rational(1,2)]*4]) + sum([1-d for d in [Rational(1,3)]*3]), 0)
checkable.asserts: Example: residues δ_μ-1 and 1-δ'_ν of d log η/dv sum to zero when Σ(1-δ_μ)=2 and Σ(1-δ'_ν)=2 (here a rectangle and an equilateral triangle), as required for an elliptic function.

transcription_corrections: Above 'Verzweigungspunkte' the image shows an interlinear insertion 'Doppel-' (written 'Doppel='), so the phrase reads 'die Doppel-Verzweigungspunkte'; the bracketed [?] can be removed.
The writer is H. A. Schwarz (same hand as the signature on the previous page); the page is a letter, not a Riemann manuscript.
Folio number '38' is written at the right margin.
